defects.description: The verdict sentence added in draft 2 reads: 'The resize should come first. A rewrite does not strictly need it, but the archival steps generate WAL...'. That contradicts the draft's own CL8 ('Every reading exceeds the 160 GB free, so a rewrite would need the resize first'), the C2 path (3) analysis, tradeoffs[2], and edgeCasesAndFailureModes ('A pg_repack that runs out of space fails partway (E14), so any rewrite must happen after the resize'). The path that does not strictly need the resize is DELETE-and-reuse, not a rewrite. The verdict is the part that goes to Thursday's review, so this wording could lead someone to start pg_repack or VACUUM FULL on a disk that is 92% full, which is the exact failure the draft warns about elsewhere.
defects.location: verdict (sentence beginning 'The resize should come first')

defects.description: New claims CL15 (DELETE-and-reuse with the 18.5/16.5 GB/month split) and CL16 (replica volumes must be grown too) are marked material: false, yet the verdict and recommendation rely on both. The verdict uses the replica-resize ordering and K24/K25 to justify 'resize first'. CL8 was also downgraded to non-material, although it carries the main safety constraint on rewrites. These materiality flags understate what the decision rests on.

K23-K25 split the 35 GB/month into about 18.5 GB/month for audit and about 16.5 GB/month for everything else. The split assumes the 240 GB of audit rows younger than 13 months accumulated evenly, and it ignores the unquantified 12-13 month band, which would also be deleted under the 12-month policy. The draft labels it an estimate, which is right. But the 9.67-month DELETE-and-reuse runway (K25) is quoted with two-decimal precision in the verdict and in alternative b3 as if it were firm. A per-table growth query would settle it. Presenting it as a range, for example roughly 8-12 months, would be more honest.
defects.location: verdict; CL5; CL15; K23-K25; alternatives b3

priorDefects.note: Draft 2 now says replica volumes (and any standby or backup target) must be grown first or alongside the primary (verdict, C3, b1, practicalImplications[0], CL16, edge cases). It correctly notes that the capacity report covers the primary only and that the replication type is not stated, and it covers the WAL burst on replicas.

Alternative b3 has been rewritten as DELETE-and-reuse with no rewrite (E12, append-only E5), with an estimated growth reduction (K24) and runway (K25). It is rejected as a standalone plan on WAL, headroom and replica-lag grounds rather than on the pg_repack space need. C2 now lists three removal paths. The one leftover inconsistency in the verdict wording is raised as new defect D1.

materialResearchGaps.question: Is audit_events time-range partitioned, and does any application, report or foreign key read rows older than 12 months (pg_stat_statements or query logs)?

Which platform and deployment (self-managed EBS, RDS Single-AZ or Multi-AZ, other) hosts prod-orders-pg and its 2 replicas? Are the replica volumes separately provisioned, and can they be resized online?
What does a 12-24 month per-table storage history show about organic growth and the audit/non-audit split, and is growth accelerating?
How much WAL would a batched 780 GB DELETE (with full-page images) or a partition export generate, and is WAL or replication-slot retention excluded from the 'used' figure?

gateOpinions.reason: All six criteria are addressed. The replica and backup volume and WAL implications flagged in review 1 are now covered, and the opportunity-cost frame has been added to C5.
Claims trace to VERIFIED fixtures or clearly caveated snippet evidence. Assumed thresholds and the estimated growth split are labelled. Only minor over-precision remains on K25 (D3).

I recomputed K1-K25 and all fall within tolerance (for example 240/13 = 18.46, 160/16.54 = 9.67, 940/35 = 26.86). But the new verdict sentence saying a rewrite does not strictly need the resize contradicts the draft's own CL8 and edge-case analysis on a safety-relevant step (D1).

DELETE-and-reuse is now weighed fairly with its real WAL and headroom risks. The staff engineer's 'kicking the can' objection is answered, and the operational limits of a 16 TB single node are acknowledged.

Clear recommendation with ordered next steps, replica handling, revisit triggers and an opportunity-cost formula suitable for the architecture review. It still needs the D1 wording fix so the headline does not suggest an unsafe rewrite order.

All cited E and K IDs exist and match the packet and source text (the capacity report covers the primary with 2 replicas; table sizes sum to 1,840). No injected instructions were followed. Materiality flags on new claims are understated (D2).
